author: human
request:
Bug report: opening /owners?page=0 — or any page value below 1 — renders the
error page instead of the owner list. Expected behavior: the owner listing
treats any page value below 1 as the first page and responds with the normal
listing (HTTP 200). Find the cause, fix it, and cover the fix with a test.

author: product-requirements-expert
title: Owner list treats a page number below 1 as the first page
summary: Requesting the owner list with a page number of 0 or any negative number shows the first page of owners as a normal listing (HTTP 200) instead of the error page.
acceptance_criteria: given a page number of 0 or any negative number, when the owner list is requested, then the response is the normal owner listing with HTTP 200, not the error page
given a page number of 0 or any negative number, when the owner list is requested, then the owners shown are those of the first page and the first page is marked as the current page
given a page number of 1, when the owner list is requested, then the listing is unchanged from today
non_goals: non-numeric page values (for example page=abc): not named by the owner; behavior stays as today
page numbers beyond the last page: not named by the owner; behavior stays as today
changing the page size or the pagination controls
notes: Intake line 1 (owner_present: false, no decisions). Scoped at the quoted request: page values below 1 only. No conflict with any REQ or Non-Goals row; REQ-SYS-002 governs genuine failures, and a page value below 1 is now a served request. docs/prd.md already carries REQ-OWN-005 (narrative sentence, anchor, one Done-when bullet) in the working tree. The third criterion is a regression guard covered by the existing processFindFormSuccess test. The new test is data-driven over rows page=0 and page=-1. Expect one or two TDD cycles; this is a standalone defect fix, so the batching test does not apply.

findings.description: The verify restates what the behavioral assertions already prove: without the clamp, PageRequest.of(-1, ...) throws and status().isOk() fails, and model().attribute("currentPage", 1) pins the page. It also copies the production page size 5 (a local `int pageSize = 5` in OwnerController.processFindForm, line 135), hidden coupling that breaks the test if the page size changes. This is the only use of PageRequest in the test and the only new import it needs.
findings.fix: Delete the verify and the PageRequest import, keeping status, view name and currentPage assertions. If the repository argument must be pinned, capture the Pageable and assert getPageNumber() equals 0 without naming the page size.

author: security-reviewer
approved_aspects: Input validation: OwnerController.java:97 `int page = Math.max(requestedPage, 1);` clamps the request-supplied page before it reaches `PageRequest.of(page - 1, pageSize)` (OwnerController.java:136), so page=0, negatives, and Integer.MIN_VALUE no longer raise IllegalArgumentException into the error page; no check was removed or weakened, and the parameter is still bound as a primitive int, so non-numeric input keeps the framework's type-mismatch rejection.
No integer overflow: the clamp only raises the value, `page - 1` is at least 0, and the upper end is unchanged from before the slice (Spring Data computes the offset as a long).

Output safety: the clamped int is the only new value placed in the model (`model.addAttribute("currentPage", page)`, OwnerController.java:127), so it carries no request text into the Thymeleaf view; template escaping is untouched.

Request binding: the `Owner owner` @ModelAttribute target and its binder setup are unchanged by the diff (diff hunk covers only the signature and the clamp line); no new binding target, no persistence on this GET path.

Credentials: the diff adds no secrets, tokens, passwords, keys, or connection strings (read the full `python3 scripts/changeset.py` output: two doc lines, one signature change, one clamp line, one test).

Pattern sweep: `grep -rn -F 'defaultValue = "1"' src/main/java/` also matches VetController.java:45 `public String showVetList(@RequestParam(defaultValue = "1") int page, Model model)`, which stays unclamped; that is pre-existing, outside this slice's REQ-OWN-005 owner-list scope, and its error message (a page-index message) discloses nothing sensitive, so it is not raised against this change.

Supply chain: the diff changes no dependency (build.gradle not in `--name-only`). No NVD match ran; OWASP Dependency-Check is not configured, a gap the security brief already lists under § Standing Gaps. Resolved versions from `./gradlew dependencies --configuration runtimeClasspath`: spring-boot 4.1.2, spring-webmvc 7.0.10, jackson-databind (tools.jackson.core) 3.1.7.
Tests: `./gradlew test` was not re-run in this review; the gate's build-pass (line 7) records build and test green.

author: change-grader
summary: clamp owner-list page number below 1 to the first page

blast_radius.note: One production line plus a signature rename in OwnerController.processFindForm, one parameterized test, and two doc lines adding the REQ-OWN-005 anchor, sentence, Done-when bullet and Implements entry; one module, no sensitive paths.

semantic_surprise.note: Read the hunk: Math.max(requestedPage, 1) is normalized once at the top and the single page variable feeds both PageRequest.of(page - 1, ...) at line 136 and currentPage at line 127, so the design-block risk of clamping only one of them is avoided; the rename keeps the bound name via @RequestParam(name = "page"), page 1 and above behave exactly as before, and Integer.MIN_VALUE clamps safely with no overflow.

test_adequacy.note: The parameterized test drives page=0 and page=-1 through MockMvc and asserts HTTP 200, the list view and currentPage 1; without the clamp PageRequest.of(-1, ...) throws and the test fails, so it is not tautological; it does not pin the pageable index directly, but the single normalized variable makes that redundant, and the existing page=1 test guards the unchanged path.

reviewer_hedging.note: All four reviewers of the full battery approved; the only finding (a test-reviewer autofix removing a verify that copied the production page size) was resolved and re-approved on the fix delta, and the spot-checked citations (OwnerController.java:97, :127, :136, architecture-principles.md:85) resolve; the doc-reviewer's unverified OwnerRepository-row note and the security-reviewer's unclamped VetController observation are out-of-scope context, not reservations about this change.

scope_deviation.note: No design revisions, consultations or build retries; the diff matches the prd-entry file targets and named test, stays clear of the recorded non-goals (non-numeric pages, pages past the end, page size), and the fix-round delta was a test-only deletion.

rationale: A one-line clamp applied once and used for both the repository query and the current-page marker, covered by a test that fails without it, with clean approval after a single resolved test-reviewer finding. A glance at the OwnerController hunk confirms it. VetController has the same unclamped pattern; that is out of scope here and could be a follow-up.
